A GEPA learning journey

Source: vignettes/articles/gepa-learning-journey.Rmd
gepa-learning-journey.Rmd

GEPA improves instructions by scoring candidate programs, showing a reflection model the failures, and asking it to rewrite the instructions. This journey uses a small support-ticket task and an offline Chat fixture so the complete path runs in documentation builds without credentials.

The fixture is deliberately scripted to make each transition predictable. Its scores show that the workflow, feedback, result fields and budget accounting work; they are not evidence that a real model improves. A live-model example and the checkpoint limits appear below.

Define the task and data splits

Route tickets as urgent when they report a current outage or compromised account, and routine otherwise. Keep the three data sets separate: GEPA sees training rows when it gathers failures for reflection, validation rows when it selects candidates, and holdout rows only for the final comparison.

library(dsprrr)
## 
## Attaching package: 'dsprrr'
## The following object is masked from 'package:stats':
## 
##     step
## The following object is masked from 'package:methods':
## 
##     signature
train <- data.frame(
  ticket = c(
    "Checkout is unavailable for every customer during an outage.",
    "Please update the billing contact.",
    "An unknown user took over my account.",
    "When is the next invoice due?"
  ),
  severity = c("urgent", "routine", "urgent", "routine")
)

validation <- data.frame(
  ticket = c(
    "A production outage is blocking every customer.",
    "A stranger gained access to my account.",
    "Can I change my billing email?"
  ),
  severity = c("urgent", "urgent", "routine")
)

holdout <- data.frame(
  ticket = c(
    "A service outage is stopping password resets.",
    "An attacker accessed my account overnight.",
    "Please add a second billing contact.",
    "Where can I see next month's invoice?"
  ),
  severity = c("urgent", "urgent", "routine", "routine")
)

program <- module(signature(
  "ticket -> severity: enum('urgent', 'routine')",
  instructions = "Use a quick baseline rule."
))

The fixture implements the small part of ellmer’s Chat protocol used here. It returns a routine label for the baseline, an outage-only proposal on its first reflection, and a complete rule after it sees feedback about the missed account-compromise case. It is only an offline teaching fixture; use an ellmer Chat constructor such as ellmer::chat_openai() in an application.

fixture_chat_class <- R6::R6Class(
  "Chat",
  public = list(
    turns = NULL,
    initialize = function(model, responder) {
      self$turns <- list()
      private$model <- ellmer::Model(name = model, extra_args = list())
      private$provider <- ellmer::Provider(name = "fixture", base_url = "")
      private$responder <- responder
    },
    chat = function(prompt, ...) {
      private$responder(paste(as.character(prompt), collapse = "\n"), NULL, ...)
    },
    chat_structured = function(prompt, type, ...) {
      private$responder(paste(as.character(prompt), collapse = "\n"), type, ...)
    },
    stream = function(...) character(),
    get_turns = function() self$turns,
    set_turns = function(turns) {
      self$turns <- turns
      invisible(self)
    },
    last_turn = function(role = NULL) NULL,
    get_model = function() private$model@name,
    get_provider = function() private$provider,
    get_model_object = function() private$model
  ),
  private = list(model = NULL, provider = NULL, responder = NULL),
  lock_objects = FALSE,
  parent_env = globalenv()
)

new_fixture_chat <- function(model, responder) {
  audit <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
  audit$prompts <- character()
  wrapped_responder <- function(prompt, type, ...) {
    prompt <- paste(as.character(prompt), collapse = "\n")
    audit$prompts <- c(audit$prompts, prompt)
    responder(prompt, type, ...)
  }
  list(
    chat = fixture_chat_class$new(model, wrapped_responder),
    audit = audit
  )
}

partial_rule <- paste(
  "Mark a ticket urgent when it reports an explicit outage;",
  "otherwise mark it routine."
)
complete_rule <- paste(
  "Mark tickets urgent when they report a current service outage",
  "or compromised account; otherwise mark them routine."
)

task_fixture <- new_fixture_chat("fixture-task", function(prompt, type, ...) {
  prompt_lines <- strsplit(prompt, "\n", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]
  input_header <- grep("^# Input:", prompt_lines)
  ticket_line <- grep("^ticket: ", prompt_lines, value = TRUE)
  if (length(input_header) != 1L || length(ticket_line) != 1L) {
    stop("Task fixture could not read one ticket from the prompt")
  }

  instructions <- paste(
    prompt_lines[seq_len(input_header - 1L)],
    collapse = "\n"
  )
  ticket <- sub("^ticket: ", "", ticket_line[[1L]])
  outage_rule <- grepl("explicit outage", instructions, fixed = TRUE) ||
    grepl("current service outage", instructions, fixed = TRUE)
  compromise_rule <- grepl("compromised account", instructions, fixed = TRUE)
  outage <- grepl(
    "outage|unavailable|blocking|stopping|down",
    ticket,
    ignore.case = TRUE
  )
  compromised <- grepl(
    "unknown user|stranger gained access|attacker|unknown login|compromised",
    ticket,
    ignore.case = TRUE
  )

  urgent <- (outage_rule && outage) || (compromise_rule && compromised)
  list(severity = if (urgent) "urgent" else "routine")
})

reflection_fixture <- new_fixture_chat(
  "fixture-reflection",
  function(prompt, type, ...) {
    account_failure <- grepl(
      "Expected urgent but got routine",
      prompt,
      fixed = TRUE
    ) && grepl(
      "An unknown user took over my account.",
      prompt,
      fixed = TRUE
    )
    instructions <- if (account_failure) {
      complete_rule
    } else {
      partial_rule
    }
    list(instructions = instructions)
  }
)

old_cache <- configure_cache(enable = FALSE)

Score the baseline

The metric returns both a score and a sentence the reflection step can use. The baseline fixture intentionally misses both urgent validation rows.

feedback_metric <- metric_with_feedback(
  function(prediction, expected) {
    correct <- identical(prediction$severity, expected$severity)
    list(
      score = as.numeric(correct),
      feedback = if (correct) {
        "Correct."
      } else {
        paste0(
          "Expected ", expected$severity, " but got ",
          prediction$severity,
          ". Check for an outage or a compromised account."
        )
      }
    )
  },
  field = "severity"
)

baseline_validation <- evaluate(
  program,
  validation,
  metric = feedback_metric,
  .llm = task_fixture$chat,
  .cache = FALSE,
  .progress = FALSE
)

baseline_validation$mean_score
## [1] 0.3333333
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(as.numeric(baseline_validation$mean_score), 1 / 3)))

data.frame(
  ticket = validation$ticket,
  expected = validation$severity,
  predicted = vapply(
    baseline_validation$predictions,
    `[[`,
    character(1),
    "severity"
  ),
  score = baseline_validation$scores
)
##                                            ticket expected predicted score
## 1 A production outage is blocking every customer.   urgent   routine     0
## 2         A stranger gained access to my account.   urgent   routine     0
## 3                  Can I change my billing email?  routine   routine     1

Run a bounded search

.llm evaluates candidate instructions. .reflection_llm proposes new instructions from training failures and their feedback. The two roles can use different models; this fixture keeps them local and deterministic. The optimizer_control() cap applies to the compile run.

task_prompt_start <- length(task_fixture$audit$prompts)
reflection_prompt_start <- length(reflection_fixture$audit$prompts)

optimized <- compile(
  program,
  GEPA(
    metric = feedback_metric,
    population_size = 2L,
    generations = 2L,
    mutation_rate = 1,
    crossover_rate = 0,
    selection = "current_best",
    seed = 42L,
    verbose = FALSE
  ),
  train,
  valset = validation,
  .llm = task_fixture$chat,
  .reflection_llm = reflection_fixture$chat,
  control = optimizer_control(
    max_metric_calls = 40L,
    progress = FALSE
  )
)

result <- optimization_result(optimized)
result
## <dsprrr_optimization_result>
## Optimizer: GEPA
## Status: completed
## Best score: 1
## Trials: 3
## Stopped: completed

The first proposal handles outages but still misses compromised accounts. The next reflection sees the failed training row and its feedback:

optimizer_task_prompts <- task_fixture$audit$prompts[
  seq.int(task_prompt_start + 1L, length(task_fixture$audit$prompts))
]
optimizer_reflection_prompts <- reflection_fixture$audit$prompts[
  seq.int(reflection_prompt_start + 1L, length(reflection_fixture$audit$prompts))
]

feedback_prompts <- optimizer_reflection_prompts[
  grepl("Feedback:", optimizer_reflection_prompts, fixed = TRUE)
]
stopifnot(
  length(feedback_prompts) > 0L,
  grepl(
    "Expected urgent but got routine",
    feedback_prompts[[1L]],
    fixed = TRUE
  ),
  grepl(train$ticket[[3L]], feedback_prompts[[1L]], fixed = TRUE)
)
feedback_lines <- strsplit(feedback_prompts[[1L]], "\n", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]
cat(grep("Feedback:", feedback_lines, value = TRUE), sep = "\n")
## Inputs: ticket: An unknown user took over my account. | Expected: urgent | Predicted: routine | Feedback: Expected urgent but got routine. Check for an outage or a compromised account.
optimizer_prompts <- paste(
  c(optimizer_task_prompts, optimizer_reflection_prompts),
  collapse = "\n"
)
stopifnot(
  !any(vapply(
    holdout$ticket,
    grepl,
    logical(1),
    x = optimizer_prompts,
    fixed = TRUE
  ))
)

The prompt audit confirms that holdout tickets did not enter candidate evaluation or reflection. They are only used after the search. The result’s GEPA extension records each candidate’s parent and validation score:

gepa_details <- result$extensions$gepa
candidate_ids <- names(gepa_details$candidates)

candidate_lineage <- data.frame(
  candidate_id = candidate_ids,
  parent = vapply(candidate_ids, function(candidate_id) {
    parents <- gepa_details$parents[[candidate_id]]
    if (length(parents) == 0L) "seed" else paste(parents, collapse = ", ")
  }, character(1)),
  validation_score = unname(gepa_details$val_aggregate_scores[candidate_ids]),
  selected = candidate_ids == result$lineage$best_candidate_id
)
candidate_lineage
##                                          candidate_id
## candidate:83ea54f4f9d988bb candidate:83ea54f4f9d988bb
## candidate:4212b0b5569dc025 candidate:4212b0b5569dc025
## candidate:54815fa4c45d5940 candidate:54815fa4c45d5940
##                                                parent validation_score selected
## candidate:83ea54f4f9d988bb                       seed        0.3333333    FALSE
## candidate:4212b0b5569dc025 candidate:83ea54f4f9d988bb        0.6666667    FALSE
## candidate:54815fa4c45d5940 candidate:4212b0b5569dc025        1.0000000     TRUE
stopifnot(
  isTRUE(any(candidate_lineage$selected)),
  isTRUE(result$best_score == 1),
  isTRUE(candidate_lineage$validation_score[
    candidate_lineage$selected
  ] == 1)
)

list(
  candidate_id = result$lineage$best_candidate_id,
  validation_score = result$best_score,
  instructions = result$best_params$component_values[[1L]]$value
)
## $candidate_id
## [1] "candidate:54815fa4c45d5940"
## 
## $validation_score
## [1] 1
## 
## $instructions
## [1] "Mark tickets urgent when they report a current service outage or compromised account; otherwise mark them routine."

Compare once on holdout

The holdout comparison is a separate evaluate() call. It does not change GEPA’s candidate selection or its recorded budget.

holdout_before <- evaluate(
  program,
  holdout,
  metric = feedback_metric,
  .llm = task_fixture$chat,
  .cache = FALSE,
  .progress = FALSE
)
holdout_after <- evaluate(
  optimized,
  holdout,
  metric = feedback_metric,
  .llm = task_fixture$chat,
  .cache = FALSE,
  .progress = FALSE
)

data.frame(
  ticket = holdout$ticket,
  expected = holdout$severity,
  before = vapply(holdout_before$predictions, `[[`, character(1), "severity"),
  after = vapply(holdout_after$predictions, `[[`, character(1), "severity")
)
##                                          ticket expected  before   after
## 1 A service outage is stopping password resets.   urgent routine  urgent
## 2    An attacker accessed my account overnight.   urgent routine  urgent
## 3          Please add a second billing contact.  routine routine routine
## 4         Where can I see next month's invoice?  routine routine routine
c(
  before = holdout_before$mean_score,
  after = holdout_after$mean_score
)
## before  after 
##    0.5    1.0
stopifnot(
  isTRUE(holdout_before$mean_score == 0.5),
  isTRUE(holdout_after$mean_score == 1)
)

The fixture score rises from 0.5 to 1.0 on these four holdout rows. This is a scripted workflow demonstration, not a real-model improvement claim. Candidate selection, feedback and results from a live search are stochastic and may not follow this path.

Read the budget and choose objectives

The public optimization result gives the compile budget and its configured limits. Here, the GEPA search used 28 metric calls from its 40-call cap. The baseline validation and two holdout evaluations below are outside that compile budget:

gepa_budget <- result$budget
stopifnot(
  isTRUE(gepa_budget$metric_calls == 28),
  isTRUE(gepa_budget$metric_calls <= gepa_budget$limits$max_metric_calls)
)
metric_accounting <- data.frame(
  phase = c(
    "GEPA compile",
    "Baseline validation",
    "Before and after holdout evaluations"
  ),
  metric_calls = c(
    gepa_budget$metric_calls,
    nrow(validation),
    2L * nrow(holdout)
  )
)
metric_accounting <- rbind(
  metric_accounting,
  data.frame(
    phase = "Total across this article",
    metric_calls = sum(metric_accounting$metric_calls)
  )
)
metric_accounting
##                                  phase metric_calls
## 1                         GEPA compile           28
## 2                  Baseline validation            3
## 3 Before and after holdout evaluations            8
## 4            Total across this article           39
stopifnot(isTRUE(metric_accounting$metric_calls[[4L]] == 39))

gepa_budget$limits$max_metric_calls
## [1] 40

This example has one objective, so candidates are ranked by that score. With several named metrics and the default selection = "pareto", GEPA ranks non-dominated trade-offs across objectives; it does not reduce them to one weighted score. selection = "current_best" instead ranks candidates only by the first metric.

The fixture does not report provider token counts or cost. With real Chats, use optimizer_control(max_provider_calls = ..., max_total_tokens = ..., max_cost = ...) to limit provider usage when the provider supplies the required measurements. Finite limits are checked between metric rows and optimizer provider calls, so the last row or call can overshoot a limit; a cost limit is not a hard provider-side spending ceiling. If a provider does not report a value, a finite cap cannot be enforced by guessing.

Where GEPA fits

  • GEPA searches candidate instructions from task failures and feedback.
  • Flex lets GEPA change a complete program source; it is a separate experimental path described in Flex: optimize a whole program.
  • Omni compares several optimizers from the same starting program and can continue from the selected result; see Compose optimizers with Omni.
  • AutoResearch and MetaHarness are outer experiment harnesses: an agent proposes edits, and dsprrr’s R evaluator validates and scores them. See Agentic optimization harnesses.

In DSPy 3.5.0, GEPA uses a native search budget chosen as exactly one of auto, max_full_evals or max_metric_calls, and its feedback metric can receive predictor and execution-trace context. dsprrr’s GEPA() exposes population_size and generations, with optional call, token, cost and time limits through optimizer_control(); metric_with_feedback() receives the prediction and expected row. Similar names do not make candidate paths or scores interchangeable. See the DSPy 3.5.0 GEPA source.

Checkpoints and an opt-in live run

GEPA checkpoint resume supports sequential round_robin searches over plain Predict leaves and built-in predictor pipelines that return plain data. It does not support Flex, other component selectors, custom module types or custom Chats, Chats with tools, or Chats with existing turns. A resume must match the original program, data, metrics, algorithm settings and effective Chat identities; resource limits may change. Completed proposals and evaluation rows are restored, but a provider request interrupted after the provider completes and before the result is committed may run again after a crash. Resume does not guarantee exactly-once provider effects. See the GEPA reference for the full contract.

To try a live search with your own labeled data, create separate task and reflection Chats and set a budget. This block is opt-in and is not run during documentation builds:

task_chat <- ellmer::chat_openai(model = "gpt-6-luna")
reflection_chat <- ellmer::chat_openai(model = "gpt-6-astra")

live_result <- compile(
  program,
  GEPA(
    metric = feedback_metric,
    population_size = 6L,
    generations = 3L,
    seed = 42L
  ),
  train,
  valset = validation,
  .llm = task_chat,
  .reflection_llm = reflection_chat,
  control = optimizer_control(
    max_metric_calls = 80L,
    max_provider_calls = 50L,
    max_cost = 1
  )
)

optimization_result(live_result)

If .reflection_llm is omitted, an explicitly supplied .llm is also used for reflection as a compatibility fallback. The reflection model proposes instructions; the task model scores them. Compare models with the same data, validation set, seed and limits, and inspect optimization_result() rather than treating a fixture score or one stochastic run as a general result.
